output.reason: A diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound now showing surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness needs hands-on wound inspection, depth/probe assessment and possible testing today, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please get your foot examined in person today (urgent care, your diabetes/foot clinic, or ED if none available). In diabetes, a spreading red, swollen, tender wound on the sole can be an infection that needs the wound looked at, probed and treated promptly. Keep weight off that foot. Go to an emergency department now if you develop fever, chills, rapidly spreading redness, black or foul-smelling tissue, or feel very unwell.
differential: Cellulitis/soft-tissue infection of a diabetic foot wound
Deeper wound infection or early diabetic foot ulcer with possible underlying involvement

redFlags.concern: Redness and swelling around foot wound
redFlags.quote: the skin around it is red and a little swollen
It's tender when I press on it.

redFlags.concern: Systemic illness, chills or high blood sugars

output.vitalSigns: No vital sign values reported; she states "No fever" but whether temperature was measured, and any other readings, are unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are consumer summaries and an ED reference synthesis, not telehealth protocols, so routing rests mainly on reported diabetic foot findings.

citations.claim: Consumer guidance advises prompt provider assessment for red, warm or painful skin on the feet in diabetes.
citations.limitation: Consumer summary; does not specify setting or timing precision.

citations.claim: Serious diabetic foot problems can develop quickly, supporting same-day rather than deferred review.
citations.limitation: General statement, not individualized risk assessment.
